data.name: NoGamesYet
data.value: No games yet. Add the folder of an installed game: the one with its .exe and .WAR files.

data.name: WelcomeText
data.value: Add the folder of an installed game (the one with its .exe and .WAR files), on this device or a memory card.

data.name: FolderGone
data.value: The folder is not there any more

data.name: FolderGoneMessage
data.value: The folder of {0} is not there any more: {1}

data.name: RemoveListOnly
data.value: Only from the list (its files and saves stay)

data.name: DeleteGone
data.value: The folder is not there any more.

data.name: DeleteNoArchives
data.value: The folder has no .WAR archives in it any more, so it was left alone.

data.name: DeleteDrive
data.value: The folder is a whole drive: it was left alone.

data.name: DeleteSystem
data.value: The folder is one of the system's own: it was left alone.

data.name: DeletePlayerData
data.value: The folder holds OpenShiina's own (saves, settings): it was left alone.

data.name: DeleteOtherGame
data.value: The folder holds another game of the list: it was left alone.

data.name: ChooseFolderTitle
data.value: Choose the folder of an installed game

data.name: CannotReadFolder
data.value: The player cannot read that folder: choose a folder on the device's storage or a memory card.

data.name: UnknownExeLooking
data.value: The game's .exe is not one the player knows: looking for the keys that open its archives…

data.name: WhichGame
data.value: These {0} games' keys all open the archives in {1}. Which game is it?

data.name: NoGameRecognised
data.value: No game was recognised in {0}: choose the folder with the game's .WAR files (no keys the player knows open them).

data.name: NeedFileAccess
data.value: OpenShiina needs access to the files to read the games: allow it, then try again.

data.name: GameNotRecognised
data.value: The game was not recognised: keep the game's own .exe in the folder, or add it again.

data.name: CouldNotPlay
data.value: Could not play the game in {0}: {1}

data.name: SettingsNote
data.value: Saved as you change them, for the next game started.

data.name: DebugNote
data.value: For bug reports: what these write goes into the game's save folder (its menu in the library opens it).

data.name: LanguageHelp
data.value: The words of OpenShiina's own screens. The games keep their own (a translation of a game changes them).

data.name: GraphicsLevelHelp
data.value: How the game's picture is scaled to the window, from the lightest to the heaviest. FSR and Anime4K run on the GPU that draws the window (without one, as Low).

data.name: CustomHelp
data.value: Set one by one under Details.

data.name: DrawingHelp
data.value: Where the games' pictures are scaled and mixed. Both give the same pictures; the GPU takes the heavy work off the processor.

data.name: NoGpu
data.value: No GPU to use ({0}): the games run on the CPU.

data.name: PaceGameHelp
data.value: As the original: up to 60 frames a second, little processor while it waits.

data.name: PaceDisplayHelp
data.value: Smoother on a fast screen, more processor.

data.name: FileCacheHelp
data.value: Memory kept for the pictures and sounds a game read, so that it does not decode them again. Bigger is smoother on scene changes and event pictures.

data.name: ThemeShiinaHelp
data.value: The logo's wine red and gold, dark.

data.name: ThemeParchmentHelp
data.value: The same colours on cream pages, light.

data.name: LevelPotatoHelp
data.value: Nearest pixels, no filtering: the least work, for the slowest phones.

data.name: LevelLowHelp
data.value: Sharp: whole game pixels, smooth only where they meet. Light.

data.name: LevelMediumHelp
data.value: FSR 1 upscaling, no sharpening: clean edges on any GPU.

data.name: LevelMaxHelp
data.value: Anime4K, made for drawn art: the heaviest, for a desktop GPU.

data.name: ProfileBatterySaverHelp
data.value: Sharp scaling at the game's own pace: the least work for the phone.

data.name: ProfilePrettyHelp
data.value: FSR 1 upscaling and sharpening, a frame every refresh of the screen: cleaner and smoother, more battery.

data.name: ScalingSharpHelp
data.value: Whole game pixels as far as they fit, the rest smooth (even text and lines).

data.name: ScalingNearestHelp
data.value: The window's size, pixels as they fall (uneven when not a whole number).

data.name: ScalingFsrHelp
data.value: AMD's upscaler, clean edges, sharpened as set below (the GPU's work).

data.name: ScalingAnime4KHelp
data.value: An upscaler made for drawn art (heaviest: a desktop GPU).

data.name: CacheAutoHelp
data.value: By the device's memory: a thirty-second of it, 64 MB to 512 MB.

data.name: CachePotatoHelp
data.value: For the oldest devices: pictures over 16 MB are read again each time.

data.name: CacheLowHelp
data.value: Light: pictures over 32 MB are read again each time.

data.name: CacheMediumHelp
data.value: Pictures of up to 64 MB are kept.

data.name: CacheHighHelp
data.value: The largest event pictures are kept too.

data.name: CacheMaxHelp
data.value: For devices with plenty of memory.

data.name: ShowFrameRateHelp
data.value: Frames a second and the slowest frame, in the window's title (on phones and tablets over the game).

data.name: GameControllerHelp
data.value: The first joystick or gamepad plays: the stick moves, button 1 decides, button 2 cancels.

data.name: PauseInBackgroundHelp
data.value: The game stands still, sound included, while another app is in front or the screen is off. Off: as the game itself says (most go on).

data.name: PauseBehindWindowsHelp
data.value: The game stands still, sound included, while another window is in front. Off: as the game itself says (most go on).

data.name: BackUpSavesHelp
data.value: Your saves and settings go into Android's backup (Google), and come back when OpenShiina is installed again or on a new phone. Android keeps 25 MB: the games played last go first.

data.name: WritePerfLogHelp
data.value: Every second, where the time went, into the game's save folder. The game runs slower while it writes.

data.name: WriteDrawTraceHelp
data.value: What every frame draws, into the game's save folder when the game ends (for reports on flicker).

data.name: TranslateX86Help
data.value: Off runs it on the interpreter instead: much slower; only to tell whether a problem comes from the translation.
